description: Services that Payload performs and sells directly: machine invocable APIs paid per call, and fixed price technical services ordered through agent marketplaces. Search by the problem you need solved. Every price and limit below is stated as it operates today.

services.capability: Hosted diagnostic actions for x402 payment failures: diagnose, failure_classification, preflight, settlement_interpretation, resolve, duplicate_payment_risk, and recover. Each action returns structured evidence and an explanation of what failed and what to do next. A free quote endpoint returns the exact price before any payment.

invocation.auth: none; the unpaid response is an x402 v2 payment requirement

invocation.note: Official MCP Registry listing. The npm package callx402 provides free local read-only tools, including x402_status.

services.limits: No guaranteed recovery and no diagnosis of every failure is promised. Settlement uses Payload's signed-redemption contract rather than the standard x402 facilitator flow. Actions named safe_retry, rescue, monitor, and execute are local-only and are not sold on the hosted rail.
services.name: callx402 hosted payment diagnostics
payment_methods: USDC on Base via the x402 payment requirements returned by the endpoint

price.note: The exact per-action amount is quoted by the free quote endpoint and in the x402 payment requirements before payment.

problems_solved: x402 payment failed
x402 payment returned an error and I do not know why
facilitator settlement failed
paid for an API call but the result never arrived
not sure whether retrying a payment is safe
possible duplicate payment
x402 receipt needs verification

services.capability: Policy preflight for proposed agent payments: signed, scoped, expiring allow, deny, or escalate decisions, plus status and usage reporting. Delivered over the rail A2A endpoint and the veyline-mcp MCP server. Governance sits outside the agent's own instructions, and the design is noncustodial.

invocation.auth: Bearer rail API key; a free key is issued at https://payload-rail.fly.dev/revrule-console/

services.limits: An authorization layer does not guarantee protection against every attack or prevent every duplicate payment. Payload does not hold customer funds, and Veyline does not provide custody, settlement, or execution. Paid subscriptions are sold through a human Stripe web checkout; there is no machine-completable purchase path.
services.name: Veyline payment preflight and spending governance

price.note: Paid plans run from $99 per month (Developer) to $5,000 per month (Enterprise) via Stripe checkout at https://payloadhq.github.io/veyline.html
price.unit: preflight evaluation with a free rail key

problems_solved: AI agent overspend
autonomous agent spent more than it should
agent payment needs approval before it runs
no spending limits on a payment enabled agent
need proof an agent payment was authorized

services.capability: Programmable revenue graphs that compute entitlements from economic events, keep an entitlement ledger, and record and verify on-chain Base USDC payout evidence against those entitlements. A keyless public evaluate endpoint runs the engine on a fixed demo graph for $0.01 USDC. A free self-serve console key runs a caller's own graphs, and event simulation is a true dry run that writes nothing.

invocation.note: Free self-serve API key for a caller's own graphs
In-browser sandbox running the real engine. Simulated; nothing moves money.

services.limits: RevRule does not execute payments and never holds funds. The keyless public evaluate endpoint evaluates a fixed demo graph, not the caller's own graph.
services.name: RevRule entitlement and payout verification
payment_methods: USDC on Base via x402 (public evaluate)

price.note: Own-graph evaluation is free with a self-serve console key. The RevRule license is $99 one time via Whop or Gumroad.
price.unit: public evaluate call on the demo graph

problems_solved: payout does not match amount owed
revenue share split needs verification

need an entitlement record before paying out
